statement: Aishah: at midday he came to Abu Bakr's house with his head covered at an unusual hour; asked that those present leave; said he had been given permission to emigrate; Abu Bakr asked for his company and he said yes.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against the full text of Bukhari 3905.

statement: Abu Bakr offered a camel; he accepted it for its price; provisions were packed in a leather bag which Asma tied with a strip of her waistband, hence 'Dhat an-Nitaqayn'.
They hired an expert guide of Banu ad-Dil who was on the religion of Quraysh; they trusted him, gave him the two camels and arranged for him to bring them to the cave of Thawr after three nights.
notes: Machine-checked. The historians name him Abdullah ibn Urayqit.

statement: The chosen men surrounded his house at night and waited until dawn, when they found Ali.
Ali slept in his bed under his green cloak and stayed behind to return the deposits people had left with the Prophet.
He left past the men unseen, reciting Qur'an 36:9.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq; the casting of dust on their heads is left out. Verse text checked in the dataset.

statement: He was fifty-three years old at the Hijrah and had spent most of those years in Makkah.
notes: Bukhari 3902: revelation at forty, thirteen years in Makkah. Revised wording accounts for his infancy with Banu Sa'd outside Makkah.

statement: Mount Thawr lies south of Makkah, the opposite direction from Yathrib.
They reached a cave in Mount Thawr and hid there for three nights.
